# fortiappseccloud_waf_template_http_header_security

Configures HTTP header security for one FortiAppSec Cloud WAF template using the static template endpoint `/waf/template/{template_id}/http_header_security`. This resource owns the template's module settings. To make an application inherit them, configure the matching app module resource with `template = true` and omit its `configs` block.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_http_header_security` resource for a WAF template.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_template_http_header_security" "example" {
  template_id = fortiappseccloud_waf_template.example.template_id

  configs {
    status                       = true
    content_security_policy      = true
    header_value                 = "default-src 'self'"
    referrer_policy              = true
    referrer_policy_header_value = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    x_content_type_options       = true
    x_frame_options              = true
    x_xss_protection             = true
  }
}
```

## Configuration Notes

- Enabling a response-header control can require its associated value. For example, enable `content_security_policy` together with `header_value` as shown.

## Argument Reference

- `template_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — WAF template ID.
- `configs` (Required) — Typed HTTP header security configuration. Its attributes and ownership-wrapper blocks are identical to `fortiappseccloud_waf_http_header_security` when that app resource uses `template = false`.

## Import

Import using the template ID:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_template_http_header_security.example TEMPLATE_ID
```

The first read after import hydrates all supported ownership wrappers.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
